meta.title: ASVAB PrepLab
meta.description: Realistic ASVAB practice in American English, with hints and explanations for non-native speakers.

home.eyebrow: Independent preparation for non-native English speakers
home.title: Master the ASVAB. Understand Every Question. Build Your Future.
home.subtitle: Prepare for the ASVAB with realistic practice tests, interactive vocabulary hints, step-by-step explanations, and personalized learning tools designed for non-native English speakers.
home.s1b: The Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery is a multiple-aptitude battery used by the U.S. military to estimate trainability and to help match applicants with occupations. PrepLab is an independent study tool. It does not enlist anyone and it does not issue an official score.
home.s2b: The subtests cover science, arithmetic word problems, word meaning, reading, high-school math, electronics, automobiles, shop tools, mechanical principles, and spatial assembly.
home.s3b: On the computer version, the next item depends on how you are doing. You cannot return to an earlier item. Each subtest has its own clock. PrepLab's adaptive mode is a training approximation, not the official psychometric algorithm.
home.s4b: The proctored CAT-ASVAB used here, without tryout items, has 135 scored questions. The paper-and-pencil version has 225 questions and 149 minutes. On paper, Auto and Shop are one combined subtest. On the computer they are separate, and the score is still reported together as AS.
home.s5b: The AFQT is built from Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, Word Knowledge, and Paragraph Comprehension. The official result is a percentile, not a raw percent correct. PrepLab shows subject accuracy and an unofficial readiness band only.
home.s6b: General Science, Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge, Electronics Information, Auto Information, Shop Information, Mechanical Comprehension, and Assembling Objects.
home.s7b: Every question stays in American English. A marked word can be opened for a meaning, a context note, and a contrast with a similar word, in English, Brazilian Portuguese, or Spanish. The hint does not select an answer for you.
home.s8b: The full simulator uses the scored CAT-ASVAB counts and time limits published by the ASVAB program, and a separate paper-and-pencil blueprint of 225 questions and 149 minutes. Hints are off unless you turn them on. If you do, the result is labeled an assisted simulation.
home.s9b: Answers, time, hint use, favorites, and spaced-review dates are stored in your account. The dashboard is calculated from those records, not from sample charts.
home.demoNote: The choices stay in English. Open the marked word to read the hint in the interface language.
home.demoContext: Context: something that exists or is available in a large amount.

practice.title: Practice by subject
practice.body: Choose one or more areas, the size of the set, the difficulty, and whether you want a clock, hints, and immediate feedback.

simulator.title: Full simulations
simulator.catBody: 135 questions and the per-section limits published for the proctored test without tryout items. You cannot go back, and the answer key stays on the server.
simulator.adaptiveBody: Same section sizes and clocks. Difficulty moves up after a correct answer and down after a miss. This is training logic, not the official CAT algorithm.
simulator.paperBody: 225 questions and 149 minutes. You can move inside the current section. Auto and Shop are one combined section.
simulator.assisted: This result is an assisted simulation because hints were used.

exam.enable: Enable hints and mark this simulation as assisted
exam.keys: Keys: 1–4 choose, N next, H hint, F flag, Esc closes a hint.

results.title: Results
results.afqtNote: This is not an official AFQT percentile. It is the accuracy on the four AFQT subjects in this session only.

dashboard.title: Your progress
dashboard.recommendBody: The weakest area with recorded answers is the best next session.
dashboard.none: Answer a few questions and this panel will use your real results.

bank.title: Question bank
bank.body: Study the validated questions in the database. Official, PDF-based, and original items can be filtered separately.
bank.emptyOfficial: No official released question is cleared for display.

review.title: Mistakes and review
review.body: Missed questions return on a spaced schedule. A miss sets the next review for the next day. Correct answers lengthen the interval.

footer.disclaimer: ASVAB PrepLab is an independent educational platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the U.S. Department of Defense or the official ASVAB Testing Program.

pages.about: PrepLab was built for candidates whose first language is not English. The questions stay in the language of the real exam. The coaching around them does not.
pages.how: You choose a subject drill, a full simulation, the whole bank, or a review of misses. Hints open only when you ask. Simulations keep the answer key on the server until the session ends.
pages.asvab: Counts and clocks follow the proctored CAT-ASVAB without tryout items and the paper-and-pencil blueprint on the official What to Expect page, checked on 18 October 2026 against the page updated 6 October 2026.
pages.privacy: The local database stores your name, email, password hash, language, answers, and study times. This build does not sell data and does not send the contact form to an outside inbox. It saves the message in the database.
pages.terms: PrepLab is a study aid. It is not an official score, not a guarantee of enlistment, and not a copy of controlled test forms. Do not share real ASVAB items. Original questions in this app are for practice.
pages.contact: Send a note. It is stored for the administrator of this installation.
pages.sources: Structure: officialasvab.com, What to Expect, updated 6 October 2026. Sample items on the official site are controlled testing materials and are not copied here. PDFs in docs are third-party files and are not published to students.
pages.sent: Your message was saved on this server.

experience.heroBody: Prepare for the ASVAB with real practice: answer in English, understand each solution in your language, and build confidence one question at a time.
experience.heroCaption: A little practice. A clearer path.
experience.whatBody: The Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery assesses verbal, math, science and technical skills. The U.S. military uses its scores for enlistment eligibility and job classification.
experience.structureNote: CAT format without experimental items. Each section has its own time limit. Original practice questions; this is not an official exam or score.
experience.waysTitle: How do you want to practice today?
experience.fullBody: Follow the sequence of all 10 sections, with a timer and results at the end. Explanations are available on request and mark your attempt as assisted.
experience.categoryBody: Select one, several or all subjects. We alternate questions across your selection, with immediate feedback and help whenever you need it.
experience.step1Body: Practice the full test or focus on the subjects you want to improve.
experience.step2Body: Choose an answer. Click an underlined word to see its meaning in your language.
experience.step3Body: Use the question-mark button for a short, clear explanation of how to reach the answer.
experience.demoTitle: Try it. Your first five questions.
experience.demoBody: Five different subjects. No timer, no account. Explore the words, answer and see why.
experience.guideBody: See what is assessed, where it appears in the test and how to approach it.
experience.accountTitle: Practice freely. Keep your progress with an account.
experience.accountBody: No login is needed to practice or take a mock test. Sign in before starting to keep your answered-question history, review mistakes and track your progress.
experience.guestNote: Guest practice is temporary and stays available in this browser for up to 24 hours. Sign in before a new session to save it to your personal history.
experience.selectionBody: Choose your subjects. We mix the questions so you can practice switching between skills.
experience.balanced: Questions are distributed evenly across your subjects, with at least one per subject. You choose the themes; we choose the questions.
experience.afqtNote: Part of the AFQT, used for enlistment eligibility.
experience.careerNote: Contributes to aptitude composites used for military job classification; requirements vary by service.
experience.simTitle: Practice the rhythm of the real test.
experience.simBody: Choose a format. Timers run separately for each section, and the answer review appears at the end. No account required.
experience.catBody: Fixed selection of original questions in official section order. No going back after answering. This mode does not adapt difficulty.
experience.adaptiveBody: Difficulty adjusts between easy, medium and hard. An educational approximation, not the official CAT algorithm.
experience.paperBody: 225 questions across 9 sections. Review answers within the current section before moving on.
experience.helpWarning: Using vocabulary or solution help marks this mock test as assisted.

GS.title: General science
GS.body: Biology, chemistry, physics and earth science.
GS.tip: Connect scientific ideas to everyday examples.

AR.title: Arithmetic reasoning
AR.body: Word problems using rates, ratios, percentages and basic operations.
AR.tip: Write down what is known, identify the unknown and check the units.

WK.title: Word knowledge
WK.body: Word meanings and synonyms in context.
WK.tip: Compare meanings, not how similar the words look.

PC.title: Paragraph comprehension
PC.body: Information, main ideas and conclusions supported by short passages.
PC.tip: Find evidence in the passage instead of using outside assumptions.

MK.title: Mathematics knowledge
MK.body: Algebra, geometry, equations and mathematical principles.
MK.tip: Simplify one step at a time and substitute your result to check it.

EI.title: Electronics information
EI.body: Electric circuits, current, voltage and electronic components.
EI.tip: Distinguish current, voltage and resistance before applying a formula.

AI.title: Auto information
AI.body: Vehicle engines, systems, maintenance and components.
AI.tip: Learn what each component does and which system it belongs to.

SI.title: Shop information
SI.body: Tools, materials, workshop techniques and safe procedures.
SI.tip: Match the tool to its purpose and pay attention to safety.

MC.title: Mechanical comprehension
MC.body: Forces, motion, levers, pulleys, gears and simple machines.
MC.tip: Sketch the forces and track the direction of motion.

AO.title: Assembling objects
AO.body: Spatial reasoning: how pieces fit together into a whole.
AO.tip: Follow corners and edges; rotate pieces mentally without mirroring them.
